title: VectorNet: Encoding HD Maps and Agent Dynamics from Vectorized Representation
layout_note: Linear left-to-right sequence that forks into two output tasks at the right end.
grouping: Five columns joined by thick grey block arrows: the scene as vectors, a column of per-polyline subgraphs, a large global graph, then a fork to two outputs (map completion above, trajectory prediction below). Colour families by element type run through every column: red for the crosswalk, blue for lanes, green for agents.
shapes_depth: The scene is drawn purely as arrow chains (red closed polygon for the crosswalk, blue arrow chains for lanes, green for agents) with plain labels. Each polyline is copied into a small dashed box and mapped by a thin arrow to a rounded tinted tile containing a three-node fully connected graph in the same colour. The global graph is a hexagon of rounded rectangle nodes, every pair joined by thin black lines. Outputs: a smaller copy of the graph with one dashed node (masked) and an 'Agent Feature' box leading to a green dashed trajectory arrow.
proposed_highlight: No box is singled out; the readable thread is the per-element colour, which stays the same from the vector drawing through its subgraph to its node in the global graph and to the predicted trajectory.
lesson: Keep each map element's colour (red crosswalk, blue lane, green agent) from its vector drawing through its local subgraph tile to its node in the global graph, so every element can be followed across stages without labels.
notes: Venue CVPR 2020 from the arXiv comment (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref). Element 'other' = the scene drawn as chains of short arrows (vectors) instead of a raster map.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: behaviour/trajectory prediction from vectorized HD maps

core.what: the scene drawn as vector polylines (crosswalk, lanes, agents), each polyline turned into a small subgraph tile and then a node of a fully connected global graph, left to right across four columns joined by thick grey block arrows

relations.form: vectorized scene -> column of dashed polyline boxes each feeding a polyline subgraph tile -> hexagonal fully connected global interaction graph -> outputs, left to right
the global graph forks into two outputs at the right: a smaller copy of the graph with one dashed node (map completion) above an agent feature box with a dashed green predicted trajectory below
each polyline is shown cut out in its own dashed box next to its three-node subgraph

channels.colour: colour = map-element identity kept through every stage: red crosswalk, blue lanes, green agents, from vector drawing to subgraph tile to global node to the predicted trajectory
channels.shape: arrows are vectors, circle-and-edge tiles are polyline subgraphs, rounded rectangles are polyline nodes in the global graph
channels.line: thick grey block arrows = stage transitions; thin black lines = graph edges; a dashed green arrow = the predicted future; a dashed node outline = the masked node to complete
channels.frame: dashed boxes isolate each input polyline; rounded tinted tiles hold each subgraph

quality.strengths: The method is drawn on a toy instance of its structure at every stage; one colour per element type carried end to end lets the reader follow any polyline without labels; the hierarchy local subgraph -> global graph is visible by position; the masked node and predicted trajectory are drawn as dashed versions of the same glyphs.
quality.weaknesses: The global graph's all-to-all edges are dense and the node features are empty boxes, so what a node holds is not shown; the 'Agent Feature' output is detached from the graph with no line showing it was read from a green node.

insights.structure: Four columns linked by thick grey block arrows: vectorized scene, a column of six dashed polyline boxes each feeding a small polyline subgraph, a fully connected global interaction graph, and two output rows (Map Completion above, Trajectory Prediction below).
insights.data: The input is a schematic of red crosswalk and blue lane and green agent polylines made of arrowed vectors; each polyline becomes a rounded tile holding a 3-node graph in its own colour, then a single coloured node in the global graph.
insights.emphasis: A consistent colour code (red crosswalk, blue lane, green agent) carries every element from raw vectors through subgraphs to global nodes, and the dashed-outline node in Map Completion marks the masked feature.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with thick grey arrows between stages; the last arrow forks into two auxiliary/main outputs.
insights.avoid: The global graph is drawn as a dense mesh of all-pairs lines that takes the biggest space but says only 'fully connected'.

arrangement.units: unframed left-to-right stages; per-polyline subgraphs in coloured rounded tiles paired with dashed polyline boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: schematic arrowed polylines labelled Crosswalk, Lane, Agent
arrangement.losses_at: right edge, as the two output tasks
